Compound Gear Drives
A compound gear drive is a type of gear train that has two or more gears mounted on 
one shaft. These gears can be mounted anywhere on the shaft, either next to each

reviewCue.excerpt:
Direction of Rotation of a Gear Drive
Each gear that is added to a gear train causes the driven gear's rotation direction to change. When 
there are only two gears, the driven gear turns in the opposite direction to the driver gear. If one gear 
is added in the middle, either an idler gear or another driven gear, the direction of rotation of the 
original driven gear will be the same as the driver gear.

reviewCue.excerpt:
Install and Align a Multiple Shaft Drive System
Each shaft in a multiple shaft drive system must be 
individually aligned. The alignment procedures for 
each shaft are the same as those for a single shaft 
drive system.
Each shaft is individually aligned, but there is a best 
order in which to align them. Start with the last 
output shaft (or the machine that can’t be 
adjusted), then work backwards toward the driver 
shaft.
Start with each shaft  0.010” to 
0.015” lower than the one 
downstream to allow for shimming 
For example, Generator 2 and the Motor 
should be aligned first and Generator 1 
and the Motor last. For the first alignment, 
the Motor is the moveable machine. For 
the second alignment, the Motor is the 
stationary machine while Generator 1 
acts as the moveable machine.

questions.answer: They do not provide flexible misalignment accommodation

reviewCue.text: Review C210 Mechanical Power Sys.pdf, slide 147. A rigid coupling makes shafts act as a single unit; misalignment places unwanted forces on shafts and bearings.
reviewCue.excerpt:
Function and Two Types of Solid Couplings: Sleeve and Flange
Solid couplings connect two shafts together to make 
them a rigid unit. They’re not commonly used
to connect motors to driven components such as pumps 
and gearboxes because they do not allow any 
misalignment. They’re only used absolute alignment is 
needed or a way to disconnect a shaft is needed.
COMPARED TO BELT, CHAIN AND GEAR 
DRIVES, RIGID COUPLINGS LIKE SLEEVE AND 
FLANGE SHOULD BE SAFER BECAUSE THEY DO 
NOT REALLY HAVE NIP or PINCH POINTS
147

questions.explanation: The sleeve is split into bolted halves that clamp around the shaft ends. It is a rigid coupling.

reviewCue.text: Review C210 Mechanical Power Sys.pdf, slide 148. The sleeve is split into bolted halves that clamp around the shaft ends. It is a rigid coupling.
reviewCue.excerpt:
Operation of Split and Sleeve Couplings
The solid sleeve coupling is a solid cylinder of metal which is designed 
to slide over the two shafts and clamp them together by means of a 
set screw on each shaft. To install this type, the two shafts must be 
able to be moved away from each other.
The split sleeve coupling clamps the two shafts together using two 
half-round pieces that clamp to each other using bolts. The split 
feature allows the two coupling halves to be removed without 
moving the two shafts away from each other.
Sleeve couplings are mainly used on smaller shafts with diameters less than six inches. Larger shafts use 
flange couplings. They are mainly used on longer shafts because these misalignments can be 
compensated by the flex allowed with longer distance between the bearings.
